# Revision 105

- Next-station names of six characters or more fit inside a fixed plate, clear of the three driving menu buttons.
- All 19 real source corridors use mapped building footprints and settlement/footprint estimates for unknown heights. Explicit mapped heights and levels take precedence. Fictional Toho remains excluded. Representative Street View references: Sasakino (2022-04), Niwasaka (2019-07), Hachioji north station deck (2016-12). This is not an individual Street View survey of every building. Imagery is not redistributed.
- User-supplied B01–B04 station ambience and city/hill/rain/snow recordings fade by station proximity, movement, settlement, weather and view. Pause/menu cleanup included. Compact mono loops preserve the deployment size allowance.
- Added heavy snow, thunderstorm, typhoon and settled snow. Thunderstorm has flashes and synthesized low thunder. Typhoon rain blows sideways.
- Snow coverage depends on mapped urban/forest density. City snow stays sparse; mountain ground and roofs accumulate more. Settled-snow and heavy-snow modes also place rounded ploughed snow banks, roughly 3–6 m high in mountain areas, below 1 m in dense cities. Banks avoid station platforms, tracks, roads, mapped buildings, bridges and tunnels.
- Typhoon places one 40 km/h temporary section ahead within the selected duty, both directions and partial runs. Existing lower limits win. HUD, lookahead, scoring and driver calls use that section; changing weather restores original limits. The supplied jyoko_1.wav slow-running cue precedes the route voice's numeric restriction call. Replay retains weather section state and speech events.
- Existing 80% wet-wheelspin acceleration / strong-brake sliding behavior is preserved.

Validation: previous suite 397/397 passed; additional snow-bank sizing test passed; browser checked long names, heavy snow, settled snow, typhoon and precipitation audio decoding. Raw archive remains below hosting limit.
